text: A PyTorch checkpoint is a flat dictionary of names ( blocks.0.attn.wq.weight ) to tensors; an NNX model's state is a nested tree of paths ( blocks/0/attn/wq/kernel ) to arrays, with every Linear weight transposed.
label: core

text: Copying by hand, one assignment per tensor, is how the silent square-matrix bug gets in.
label: core

text: Write the conversion as a rule on the path , apply it to every leaf, and let shape checks fail loudly.
label: core

text: Here the whole rule is a four-entry table: kernel becomes weight and is transposed; bias , scale (to weight ) and embedding (to weight ) are copied.
label: core

text: The file in between is safetensors : a JSON header (names, dtypes, shapes, byte offsets) followed by raw bytes, readable by torch, numpy and JAX, with no pickle and so no code executed on load. def torch_name(path): # ('blocks', 0, 'attn', 'wq', 'kernel') -> ('blocks.0.attn.wq.weight', True) *mods, leaf = [str(p) for p in path] tname, transpose = {"kernel": ("weight", True), "bias": ("bias", False), "scale": ("weight", False), "embedding": ("weight", False)}[leaf] return ".".join(mods + [tname]), transpose flat_in = safetensors.flax.load_file("tinylm_torch.safetensors") # {name: jax.Array} state = nnx.state(model, nnx.Param) leaves = [] for path, var in nnx.to_flat_state(state): name, tr = torch_name(path) w = flat_in[name].T if tr else flat_in[name] assert w.shape == var[...].shape, (name, w.shape, var[...].shape) # the check a hand copy forgets leaves.append((path, var.replace(w))) nnx.update(model, nnx.from_flat_state(leaves)) From src/runs/pj_convert.py , run on the running example's 500-step weights.
label: core
